chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibnillah Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shamar, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When Noah (peace be upon him) supplicated to his Lord, the Exalted, against his people, Satan (may God curse him) came to him and said: 'O Noah, I have a favor owed to you, and I wish to repay it.' Noah said: 'By God, I dislike that you have a favor owed to me; what is it?' He said: 'Yes, you called upon God against your people and He drowned them, so no one remained whom I had led astray; thus I am at ease until another generation arises, and I will lead them astray.' Noah said to him: 'What do you want me to repay you with?' He said to him: 'Remember me in three situations, for I am closest to the servant when he is in one of them: Remember me when you are angry, and remember me when you judge between two people, and remember me when you are alone with a woman with no one else present.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three situations in which Satan is closest to humans according to the hadith of Noah and Satan?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Satan claims a reciprocal favor from Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) for his prayer that led to the drowning of his disbelieving people, thereby sparing that generation from his influence. Satan requests to be remembered in three specific states—anger, judgment, and solitude with a woman—as these are moments when he gains the strongest hold over the human soul. This highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of how divine decree and human agency intersect in the cosmic struggle between good and evil.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-140 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Aba Abdullah Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqy, on the authority of Ahmad ibn an-Nazr, on the authority of Amr ibn Shimr, on the authority of Jabir that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) said,

“When Noah (MGB) prayed to his Lord - the Honorable the Exalted God - and cursed his nation, Satan - May God damn it - said, ‘O Noah! I am indebted to you and wish to give you a reward.’ Noah said, ‘I swear by God that you do not owe me anything. What could it be?’ Satan said, ‘I am indebted to you since you did me a favour by your praying to God to drown everyone in your nation. Now until there comes another generation, no one is left to need my leading him astray.’ Noah said, ‘Yes. What reward do you want to give me?’ Satan said, ‘Remember me in three situations where I am closest to my servants: whenever you get angry; whenever you want to judge between two people and remember me whenever you are left alone with another unfamiliar woman. ”
